successors.name: Mahan confederacy
successors.text: Mahan, the south-west and the Han valley

successors.name: Jinhan confederacy
successors.text: Jinhan, the south-east east of the Nakdong

ledger.x: 197 BCE: Jin enters the map in the south of the peninsula.
92 BCE: Jin's land divides into the Samhan.
92 BCE: Jinhan emerges from Jin; the Records of the Three Kingdoms say 'Jinhan succeeded Jin'.
92 BCE: Byeonhan emerges from Jin; the Book of the Later Han says Mahan, Jinhan and Byeonhan 'were all part of the former Jin state'.
92 BCE: Jin gives way to the three Han confederacies.

certainty.note: The page gives no frontier and no capital; the Cliopatria shape is a core of the south.
